content:
- Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in the early part of the 30-day window.
- Forecasts tend to be too low relative to recent high values, suggesting underreaction to recent spikes.
- After a spike in true values, forecasts often overshoot slightly but then fall back — indicating a lag in adjusting to new highs.
- Model shows weak mean reversion; prices often stay elevated longer than forecast suggests.
- Forecasts are overly conservative in the first 5–10 days, then gradually increase — suggesting a delayed response to recent trends.
- Model fails to capture the magnitude of late-period spikes (e.g., 36.62, 38.18) — underestimates volatility in final 5–10 days.
- Forecast mean is typically 1–2 points below true mean, indicating persistent downward bias.
- Forecasts often lag behind true values by 1–3 days, especially in the first 10 days of the forecast horizon.
